description: Test your knowledge of Male external genitalia anatomy, structure, and clinical correlations for MBBS students.

cards.text: What are the dimensions of the testis and what produces testosterone?
cards.answer: Testis is ~5×3×3 cm. Leydig (interstitial) cells lying between seminiferous tubules produce testosterone.

tip.tip: Leydig = Leydig cells = Testosterone. Located in the interstitium (between the tubules).

cards.text: How many seminiferous tubules are in each testis, and at what temperature does spermatogenesis occur?
cards.answer: ~250 lobules, each containing 1-4 seminiferous tubules. Spermatogenesis occurs at 35°C (below normal body temperature).

tip.tip: Cool testis = Spermatogenesis. That's why the scrotum is external—temperature regulation is critical.

cards.text: Which testicular covering is a potential space and what clinical condition can develop there?
cards.answer: The tunica vaginalis (visceral and parietal layers) creates a potential space where fluid can accumulate, forming a hydrocele.

tip.tip: Tunica Vaginalis = Vaginalis cavity = Hydrocele fluid space. Think 'vaginal sac around testis.'

cards.text: Describe testicular descent: what guides it and when is it complete?
cards.answer: The gubernaculum testis (mesenchymal cord) guides descent from the retroperitoneum (L1-L2) through the inguinal canal. Normally reaches scrotum by birth.

tip.tip: Gubernaculum = 'guide rope.' Descent occurs 7th-9th months gestation. If not by 1 year = cryptorchidism.

cards.text: What is the anatomical relationship of the epididymis to the testis, and how long does sperm maturation take?
cards.answer: Epididymis lies on the posterolateral surface in three parts (head, body, tail). Sperm maturation takes ~12 days as they transit through the ~7 m coiled duct.

tip.tip: Epididymis = Comma-shaped, always POSTERIOR. A 12-day journey from immotile to motile sperm.

cards.text: How do you differentiate epididymitis from testicular torsion on clinical examination?
cards.answer: Cremaster reflex is PRESERVED in epididymitis but ABSENT in testicular torsion. Stroking inner thigh causes testis to rise in epididymitis but not in torsion.

tip.tip: Cremaster reflex = Cremasteric muscle (from internal oblique). Present = Epididymitis. Absent = Torsion (surgical emergency).

cards.text: On what structure is vasectomy performed, and where is this structure located?
cards.answer: Vasectomy is performed on the vas deferens (ductus deferens), which is continuous with the tail of the epididymis and is palpable through scrotal skin at the lower pole.

tip.tip: Vas = 'vessel' carrying sperm. Palpable through skin—safe to locate and divide without affecting blood supply.

cards.text: Identify the three erectile bodies of the penis and their arrangement.
cards.answer: Two dorsal corpora cavernosa (paired, joined by incomplete septum) and one ventral corpus spongiosum (surrounds urethra). Together they form the erectile tissue.

tip.tip: 2 CAVErnosa (dorsal, paired) + 1 SPONGiosum (ventral, single). SpongiosumSurrounds the SPONge-like urethra.
